honoured_table.target_citation: Cal. Pub. Util. Code 454.53(a): 'It is the policy of the state that eligible renewable energy resources and zero-carbon resources supply 90 percent of all retail sales of electricity to California end-use customers by December 31, 2035, 95 percent ... by December 31, 2040, [and] 100 percent ... by December 31, 2045.'  Subdivision (b)(4) disclaims any effect on enforcement against retail sellers, which is why the central does not carry it.
honoured_table.citation: Cal. Pub. Util. Code 399.15(b)(2)(B) - retail sellers shall procure eligible renewable energy resources equal to 44 percent of retail sales by 2024-12-31, 52 percent by 2027-12-31, 60 percent by 2030-12-31, and 'not less than 60 percent of retail sales' in every subsequent compliance period; penalties under 399.15(b)(8). SEPARATELY Cal. Pub. Util. Code 454.53(a) states 90/95/100 percent by 2035/2040/2045 as 'the policy of the state', and 454.53(b)(4) provides that it does not affect the rules and requirements for enforcement against retail sellers under the Renewables Portfolio Standard Program.

honoured_table.target_citation: C.R.S. 40-2-125.5(3)(a)(II): for 2050 and thereafter a qualifying retail utility 'shall seek to achieve the goal' of 100 percent clean energy 'so long as doing so is technically and economically feasible, in the public interest'.  The section is captioned 'goal to eliminate by 2050'.  The separate 80 percent carbon dioxide reduction by 2030 at 40-2-125.5(3)(a)(I) is measured against 2005 emissions and is not a share, so it is not honoured.
honoured_table.citation: C.R.S. 40-2-124(1)(c)(I)(E) - the electric resource standards shall require each qualifying retail utility to generate or cause to be generated 30 percent of its retail electricity sales in Colorado from eligible energy resources for 2020 and thereafter (cooperatives 20 percent, municipal utilities serving more than 40,000 customers 10 percent, under 40-2-124(1)(c)(V)). SEPARATELY C.R.S. 40-2-125.5(3)(a)(I) - by 2030 a qualifying retail utility shall reduce carbon dioxide emissions associated with electricity sales by 80 percent from 2005 levels; 40-2-125.5(3)(a)(II) - for 2050 and thereafter the utility 'shall seek to achieve the GOAL' of 100 percent clean energy 'so long as doing so is technically and economically feasible, in the public interest'. The section heading itself reads 'goal to eliminate by 2050'.

honoured_table.target_citation: 20 ILCS 3855/1-75(c)(1)(B): the Agency 'shall attempt to procure' renewable energy resources equal to 50 percent of the applicable utilities' load by delivery year 2040, above the 40 percent that is the enforceable requirement from delivery year 2030.
honoured_table.citation: 415 ILCS 5/9.15(g)-(k) (Climate and Equitable Jobs Act, P.A. 102-0662): private coal and oil units shall permanently reduce all CO2e and copollutant emissions to zero no later than 2030-01-01; private gas units on a staged schedule ending '(5) No later than January 1, 2045: all remaining EGUs and large greenhouse gas-emitting units'; public coal units to zero no later than 2045-12-31; public gas and cogeneration units by 2045-01-01. PLUS 20 ILCS 3855/1-75(c)(1)(B) - renewable procurement rising to at least 40 percent by the 2030 delivery year and continuing at no less than 40 percent thereafter (the Agency 'shall attempt to procure' 50 percent by delivery year 2040).

honoured_table.target_citation: IC 8-1-37 (voluntary clean energy portfolio standard program): the clean energy portfolio standard goal is 10 percent of a participating utility's total retail electricity supply by 2025.  Participation is elective, which is why the central does not carry it.
honoured_table.citation: IC 8-1-37 (voluntary clean energy portfolio standard program; participation is elective and the 10 percent by 2025 figure is a goal, not an obligation)

honoured_table.target_citation: 35-A M.R.S. 3210(1-A): state goals of 80 percent of retail electricity sales from renewable resources by 2030 and 90 percent renewable plus 10 percent clean by 2040.  Both rungs sit at or below the sum of Maine's enforceable portfolio requirements, so honouring them adds no rung to Maine's floor.
honoured_table.citation: 35-A M.R.S. 3210: subsection 3 - no less than 30 percent of the portfolio from Class II resources; subsection 3-A(A)(10) - 10 percent Class I for 2017 and each year thereafter; subsection 3-B(A) - Class IA rising to 40 percent in 2030 and 'Fifty percent for the period from January 1, 2040 to December 31, 2040 and each year thereafter' [PL 2025, c. 386, sec. 7]; subsection 3-D(A) - Class III ('clean resource', which includes nuclear and hydroelectric) rising from 1 percent in 2031 to 10 percent in 2040 and each year thereafter [PL 2025, c. 386, sec. 8]. The four are additive: resources used for one may not be used for another.

honoured_table.target_citation: G.S. 62-110.9: 'The Utilities Commission shall take all reasonable steps to achieve reduction in emissions of carbon dioxide ... that result in carbon neutrality by the year 2050'; the section calls this 'the authorized carbon reduction goal' throughout and permits offsets up to 5 percent.  Carbon neutrality is honoured here as a clean share of one, which is the reading the bound is asked to take and is more than the statute's own words guarantee.
honoured_table.citation: G.S. 62-133.8(b)(1) - each electric public utility shall be subject to a Clean Energy and Energy Efficiency Portfolio Standard of '12.5% of 2020 North Carolina retail sales' for 2021 and thereafter (electric membership corporations and municipalities 10 percent of 2017 sales from 2018); up to 40 percent of the requirement may be met with energy efficiency savings from 2021, and up to 25 percent with out-of-state renewable energy certificates. SEPARATELY G.S. 62-110.9 - 'The Utilities Commission shall take all reasonable steps to achieve reduction in emissions of carbon dioxide ... that result in carbon neutrality by the year 2050'; the section calls this 'the authorized carbon reduction goal' throughout and permits offsets up to 5 percent.

honoured_table.target_citation: NMSA 1978, 62-16-4 (Energy Transition Act): for rural electric cooperatives the 2050 zero-carbon figure is a target conditioned on technical feasibility and reliability, not the mandate that binds public utilities at 2045.  It sits at the level New Mexico's enforceable floor already reaches five years earlier, so honouring it adds no rung.
honoured_table.citation: NMSA 1978, 62-16-4(A) (Energy Transition Act, 2019 SB 489, sec. 29) - for public utilities other than rural electric cooperatives and municipalities: (3) no later than 2025-01-01, renewable energy shall comprise no less than 40 percent of total retail sales; (4) no later than 2030-01-01, no less than 50 percent; (5) no later than 2040-01-01, renewable energy resources shall supply no less than 80 percent of all retail sales of electricity in New Mexico; (6) no later than 2045-01-01, ZERO CARBON RESOURCES shall supply one hundred percent of all retail sales of electricity in New Mexico. For rural electric cooperatives the corresponding 2050 zero-carbon figure is a TARGET, conditioned on technical feasibility and reliability.

honoured_table.target_citation: NRS 704.7820(2): it is the policy of this State to become a leading producer and consumer of clean and renewable energy, 'with a goal of achieving by 2050 an amount of energy production from zero carbon dioxide emission resources equal to the total amount of electricity sold by providers of electric service in this State'.
honoured_table.citation: NRS 704.7821(1) - the portfolio standard for each provider: (j) for calendar years 2024 through 2026, not less than 34 percent; (k) for 2027 through 2029, not less than 42 percent; (l) 'For calendar year 2030 and for each calendar year thereafter, not less than 50 percent of the total amount of electricity sold by the provider to its retail customers in this State during that calendar year.' SEPARATELY NRS 704.7820(2) - it is the policy of this State to become a leading producer and consumer of clean and renewable energy, 'with a GOAL of achieving by 2050 an amount of energy production from zero carbon dioxide emission resources equal to the total amount of electricity sold by providers of electric service in this State'.

honoured_table.target_citation: SDCL 49-34A-101: 'There is hereby established a state renewable, recycled, and conserved energy objective that ten percent of all electricity sold at retail within the state by the year 2015 be obtained from renewable, recycled, and conserved energy sources. ... This objective is voluntary, and there is no penalty or sanction for a retail provider of electricity that fails to meet this objective.'  The stated year precedes the first projected year, so the honoured floor takes effect at 2025.

honoured_table.target_citation: Utah Code 54-17-602(1)(a): 'To the extent that it is cost effective to do so, beginning in 2025 the annual retail electric sales in this state of each electrical corporation shall consist of qualifying electricity or renewable energy certificates in an amount equal to at least 20% of adjusted retail electric sales.'  The cost-effectiveness condition is why the central does not carry it.

ruling_D6.rule: x(t) = 1 - (1 - x2050) exp(-k (t-2050)), k = s2050 / (1 - x2050), for t > 2050; the 2050 value is held where s2050 <= 0.  The ruling-D5 statutory floors apply on top.
